My PhD asks how social contact, mobility and attitude data can be used
to understand and help anticipate the behavioural drivers of epidemic dynamics. It
builds on a background in mathematics and health data science, and on earlier
work using branching process models to estimate the probability that an
introduction becomes a major epidemic.

I also work in health economics, on screening for blood-borne viruses.
